summary: The line about people trying to survive in a universe with a "morbid sense of humor" gets the movie perfectly. It is bleak, pitiless, and weirdly sad about how revenge keeps spreading damage outward.
good_pick_if: you want a hard-edged thriller with moral wreckage, not catharsis
maybe_skip_if: you want anyone to get out of this feeling okay

source_quotes.text: a universe that has a morbid sense of humor

summary: "Kafka’s metamorphosis but bisexual" is a funny but useful pitch. The movie plays like a neon panic attack full of horny confusion, apocalypse vibes, and queer chaos that somehow never stops being alive.
good_pick_if: you want something messy, loud, and genuinely one of a kind
maybe_skip_if: you want narrative stability or tonal control

summary: The phrase "action as emotionality" is exactly why this lands. Every fight feels like feeling made physical, and the color-driven visual design gives the whole movie a mythic, painterly calm.
good_pick_if: you want martial-arts spectacle that feels graceful, not just loud
maybe_skip_if: you want a rougher or more grounded action movie

summary: That line about heads exploding while "Wang Chung is playing" gets the lurid appeal. It is pure neon sleaze and reckless momentum, the kind of eighties crime movie that feels dangerous and stylish at once.
good_pick_if: you want a crime thriller with heat, attitude, and grime
maybe_skip_if: you want cops played as clean heroes

summary: Once somebody quotes "It takes a lot to make a stew," you know the bit has already worked. The short just keeps pushing one dumb TV theme into a full nightmare until the repetition becomes the joke and the horror.
good_pick_if: you want something short, absurd, and increasingly cursed
maybe_skip_if: repetition-based comedy turns irritating fast for you

source_quotes.text: It takes a lot to make a stew.

summary: Calling Popeye Doyle the "all-time NYPD MVP" is one way of saying the movie runs on ugly, relentless drive. It still feels hard, dirty, and physically immediate in a way a lot of crime movies do not.
good_pick_if: you want a crime classic that feels raw instead of museum-safe
maybe_skip_if: you want polished charm from your antiheroes

source_quotes.text: Popeye Doyle is the all-time NYPD MVP.

summary: "Fuck Bombers never die!" is exactly the kind of deranged devotion this movie inspires. It is a movie-about-movies bloodbath powered by pure enthusiasm, where filmmaking itself feels like a combat sport.
good_pick_if: you want something maximal, funny, and aggressively alive
maybe_skip_if: you want tonal restraint or tidy realism

summary: The "zombies on a train > snakes on a plane" take is reductive but fair. The movie absolutely rips as contained panic, and it still finds room for real emotion instead of treating the whole ride like disposable chaos.
good_pick_if: you want a propulsive horror movie that also gets emotional
maybe_skip_if: you want your zombie movies colder or gorier

source_quotes.text: zombies on a train > snakes on a plane

summary: The best short review note here is that Willem Dafoe was "being robbed of awards." The movie lands because the performances make the jungle feel morally split, sweaty, and violently immediate instead of abstract.
good_pick_if: you want a war movie that feels raw and spiritually scorched
maybe_skip_if: you want a less brutal or less chaotic battle portrait

source_quotes.text: Willem Dafoe was being robbed of awards.

summary: The joke that it "does for potatoes what Oppenheimer did for the atomic bomb" is funny because the movie really does turn stubborn agricultural ambition into something huge, tense, and unexpectedly metal.
good_pick_if: you want a historical drama with muscle and a revenge streak
maybe_skip_if: you want something softer or less grimly driven

source_quotes.text: Does for potatoes what Oppenheimer did for the atomic bomb.
